subject: Post-demo: prompt set collection + recommended models / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@acme.com>, Rahul Patel <rahul.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: prompt set collection + recommended models / next steps

Hi Jamie / Rahul —

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really helpful to see the multi-turn summarization and the redaction-sensitive flow you walked through. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on model fit and run an initial eval: 

- Summary: primary use case is transactional email summarization + PII redaction for your support automation (avg convo length ~8 turns, median tokens ~420). You also flagged an edge case around legal disclaimers and attachments.
- Recommended model variants (initial): rw-open-3b-8k-quant (fast, cost-efficient) and rw-open-7b-16k-quant (higher quality for long threads); fallback: rw-open-7b-32k for the longest threads.
- Suggested benchmarks: we’ll run our standard summarization + redaction suite and add your prompt set (see request below).

Can you please: 1) share a representative sample of user prompts/conversations (redact or replace PII where needed) — ideally 50–100 examples in CSV with columns: conversation_id, role, message, expected_summary, redaction_flags; 2) flag any edge cases (attachments, HTML emails, non-English snippets); 3) permission to include up to 30 de-identified items in our eval benchmark report.

We’ve attached a template CSV and a short note about redaction guidance. No need to be exhaustive — we mainly want samples that capture the tricky behaviors you care about (legal disclaimers, signatures embedded in bodies, quoted text). When you send the CSV, please indicate which rows are ‘high-priority’ for quality.

Plan on our side: Aditya will provision a cost/latency matrix for the two model variants and Rishi will kick off the security/compliance checklist. I’ll ingest the prompt set and run the first-pass eval; we’ll aim to share results within 5 business days after we receive the sample.

Next sync: suggest 30-min follow-up on Aug 18 to review initial evals — does that work?

Thanks —

— Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Attachments: acme_prompt_samples_template.csv (stub), redaction_guidance.txt (stub)
From: Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rahul Patel <rahul.patel@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: prompt set collection + recommended models / next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is great and aligns with our goals. A couple quick clarifications before we pull the sample set together: 

1) For PII redaction, can you confirm what you consider acceptable redaction vs. pseudonymization for the eval data? We can replace names with initials but need to ensure it still exercises named-entity redaction.
2) On attachments: we have a mix of PDFs and inline HTML. Do you want us to extract text first or include attachments as separate rows describing the attachment content?

We’ll start compiling ~75 examples and mark ~20 as high-priority. I’ll loop in our privacy lead if needed but we should be able to de-identify per your guidance.

Also — happy to go with the Aug 18 follow-up.

— Jamie
Senior Product Manager, Acme Corp
jamie.lee@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: prompt set collection + recommended models / next steps

Hi Jamie —

Great questions — short answers below and detailed notes attached.

1) Redaction guidance: acceptable options are full redaction (REDACTED), deterministic pseudonyms (User_123), or hashed ids. For eval, deterministic pseudonyms are preferable because they preserve entity consistency across turns and let us test co-reference redaction without exposing raw PII. Please avoid free-form initials where possible. 

2) Attachments: if you can extract the text and provide a short attachment_summary column that we can match to the thread row, that’s ideal. If extraction isn’t possible, include a row per attachment with a short description and a note about file type (pdf/html).

I’ve attached: acme_prompt_samples_template.csv (template), redaction_guidance.txt (detailed examples), and a copy of our eval benchmark summary (redwood_eval_benchmarks_2026.pdf) to show the metrics we’ll report (ROUGE, hallucination rate, redaction recall/precision).

When you send the samples, include a quick note listing the top 5 concerns you want prioritized (e.g., legal disclaimers, embedded signatures, multilingual snippets). We’ll use those to weight the evaluation and highlight regressions.

Thanks — we’ll review as soon as it arrives.

— Marissa
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Rahul Patel <rahul.patel@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: prompt set collection + recommended models / next steps

Marissa / team —

We’ve prepared the sample set and attached a CSV. A couple of notes: 

- The CSV includes 78 rows (conversations) with an attachments_summary column for the 12 items that had attachments. We redacted names to deterministic pseudonyms per your guidance (User_001, User_002).
- We included 7 edge cases flagged in the "notes" column: legal disclaimers, HTML signature blocks, pasted PDF content, Spanish/Portuguese snippets, and conversations with long quoted history.
- Quick privacy question: can you confirm that any raw content used for the eval report will be stored in our dedicated project workspace and not exposed externally? We prefer the dedicated workspace and a short retention window (30 days) for eval artifacts.

Let me know if anything else is needed. Jamie — we tagged 20 rows as high-priority.

Thanks,
Rahul
CTO, Acme Corp
Attachments: acme_prompt_samples.csv (stub)
